meta.note: company_tags indicative hain (frequently asked trends), official guarantee nahi.

theory.concept: Ek pointer read karta hai (i), doosra write (k). Condition satisfy karne wale elements ko a[k++] par likho. 'At most 2 duplicates' jaisi problems me condition x != a[k-2] ban jati hai.
key_points: Remove Duplicates (at most 1): compare with a[k-1]; at most 2: compare with a[k-2]
Compression me output hamesha input se chhota ya barabar hota hai, isliye same array me likhna safe hai
Read pointer hamesha write pointer se aage ya barabar rehta hai (invariant)
Ek baar likhne ke baad us jagah ko dobara padhna nahi hota
pitfalls: Write pointer ko read pointer se aage nikal dena
Count ke digits (10+ run length) ko ek hi character samajhna

theory.concept: Sorted array me answer ko har step par aadha kar dena. Search space [lo, hi] me mid check karo aur ek half discard karo. Time O(log n). Level 2 me ye 'binary search on answer' tak jata hai.
key_points: mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2 (lo + hi overflow kar sakta hai)
Loop condition lo <= hi, aur update lo = mid + 1 / hi = mid - 1 (infinite loop se bachne ke liye)
Integer sqrt: 'sabse bada mid jiska mid*mid <= x' ek monotonic condition hai
Monotonic condition (false...false true...true) ho to binary search lag sakta hai
pitfalls: mid*mid int me overflow (long long use karo)
hi = n instead of n-1 ka confusion

theory.concept: Divisors pairs me aate hain (i, n/i), isliye sirf sqrt(n) tak check karna kaafi hai. LCM(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b (pehle divide karo, overflow kam hota hai).
key_points: Perfect number: proper divisors ka sum n ke barabar (6, 28, 496)
LCM of array = fold: l = lcm(l, a[i])
Armstrong number: digits ka (digit count)-th power ka sum number ke barabar
Integer sqrt ke liye linear O(sqrt x) ya binary search O(log x), floating sqrt() par precision risk
pitfalls: i * i int overflow (long long cast)
Perfect square par i aur n/i ko do baar jodna
pow() ka double result integer me galat round ho sakta hai

theory.concept: Ye problems chhote helper skills test karti hain: case check, run-length grouping, multiset counting, word-wise operations.
key_points: isupper/islower/toupper/tolower ko (unsigned char) cast karke call karo
Run grouping: j = i; while(j < n && s[j] == s[i]) j++;
Target word ke liye frequency/requirement: balloon = b1 a1 l2 o2 n1, answer = min(count / need)
Word-wise reverse: har word ke start/end indices nikalo aur segment reverse karo
pitfalls: Words ke beech multiple spaces (problem statement check karo)
Count 1 ho to number mat likho (compression)
char ko int index banate waqt negative index

theory.concept: Recursion me har call ki apni cost hoti hai. s.substr() har baar naya string copy karta hai, to O(n) recursion calls * O(n) copy = O(n^2). Indices pass karo (reference + l, r) to O(n) rehta hai.
key_points: Tribonacci: 3 branches => naive O(3^n); iterative 3 variables O(n) time O(1) space
String ko by-value pass karna bhi copy hai; const string& ya index use karo
Recursion depth ~1e5 par stack overflow ka risk; iterative convert karna safe
Base case + progress (problem chhota hota hai) dono ensure karo
pitfalls: Overlapping subproblems par memo/DP na lagana

problems.title: Maximum Product of Three Numbers
problems.problem_statement: Given an integer array, find three numbers whose product is maximum and return that product.
problems.description: Negative numbers ki wajah se do bade negatives aur ek bada positive bhi maximum product de sakte hain.
problems.theory: Answer ya to teen sabse bade ka product hota hai, ya do sabse chhote (most negative) aur ek sabse bade ka product.

brute_force.approach: Teen nested loops se har triplet ka product.
brute_force.code_cpp: int maxProd3(const vector<int>& a){ int n = a.size(), best = INT_MIN; for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) for(int k = j + 1; k < n; k++) best = max(best, a[i] * a[j] * a[k]); return best; }

optimized.approach: Ek pass me 3 maximum aur 2 minimum track karo.
optimized.code_cpp: int maxProd3(const vector<int>& a){ int mx1 = INT_MIN, mx2 = INT_MIN, mx3 = INT_MIN, mn1 = INT_MAX, mn2 = INT_MAX; for(int x : a){ if(x > mx1){ mx3 = mx2; mx2 = mx1; mx1 = x; } else if(x > mx2){ mx3 = mx2; mx2 = x; } else if(x > mx3) mx3 = x; if(x < mn1){ mn2 = mn1; mn1 = x; } else if(x < mn2) mn2 = x; } return max(mx1 * mx2 * mx3, mn1 * mn2 * mx1); }

problems.explanation: Sort karke bhi ho jata hai (O(n log n)): max(a[n-1]*a[n-2]*a[n-3], a[0]*a[1]*a[n-1]). Interview me ye observation (two negatives) hi asli test hai.

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II (At Most Twice)
problems.problem_statement: Given a sorted array, remove duplicates in-place so that each element appears at most twice. Return the new length k.
problems.description: O(1) extra space, relative order same.
problems.theory: Write pointer k. Element x ko tabhi likho jab k < 2 ho ya x != a[k-2]. Ye 'at most m duplicates' ka general template hai (m = 2 par a[k-2], m par a[k-m]).

brute_force.approach: Ek jaisi teen values milne par vector se erase karo.
brute_force.code_cpp: int removeDup2(vector<int>& a){ int i = 2; while(i < (int)a.size()){ if(a[i] == a[i-1] && a[i] == a[i-2]) a.erase(a.begin() + i); else i++; } return a.size(); }

optimized.code_cpp: int removeDup2(vector<int>& a){ int k = 0; for(int x : a) if(k < 2 || x != a[k-2]) a[k++] = x; return k; }

problems.explanation: Erase har baar shifting karta hai (O(n)), isliye O(n^2). a[k-2] compare isliye kaam karta hai ki sorted array me teesra duplicate wo hi hoga jo a[k-2] ke barabar ho.

problems.title: Two Sum II (Sorted Array)
problems.problem_statement: Given a sorted array, find two numbers that add up to target. Return their 1-based indices [i, j] with i < j.
problems.description: Exactly ek solution hai aur O(1) extra space chahiye (sorted hone ka fayda uthao).
problems.theory: l = 0, r = n-1. Sum chhota ho to l++, bada ho to r--. Sorted hone se kabhi galat discard nahi hota.

brute_force.code_cpp: vector<int> twoSumSorted(const vector<int>& a, int t){ int n = a.size(); for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) if(a[i] + a[j] == t) return {i + 1, j + 1}; return {}; }

optimized.code_cpp: vector<int> twoSumSorted(const vector<int>& a, int t){ int l = 0, r = (int)a.size() - 1; while(l < r){ int s = a[l] + a[r]; if(s == t) return {l + 1, r + 1}; if(s < t) l++; else r--; } return {}; }

problems.explanation: Unsorted me Two Sum ke liye hash map lagta hai (O(n) space). Sorted array me two pointers se O(1) space milti hai.

problems.title: Insertion Sort
problems.problem_statement: Sort an array in ascending order using insertion sort.
problems.description: Left part hamesha sorted rehta hai; naya element us sorted part me sahi jagah par daala jata hai.
problems.theory: key = a[i]; sorted part me bade elements ko ek jagah right shift karo; khali jagah par key rakho. Stable sort hai.

brute_force.approach: Adjacent swap se element ko peeche tak le jao.
brute_force.code_cpp: void insertionSort(vector<int>& a){ for(int i = 1; i < (int)a.size(); i++) for(int j = i; j > 0 && a[j-1] > a[j]; j--) swap(a[j], a[j-1]); }

optimized.approach: Shifting: key ko hold karo, shift karo, ek baar write.
optimized.code_cpp: void insertionSort(vector<int>& a){ for(int i = 1; i < (int)a.size(); i++){ int key = a[i], j = i - 1; while(j >= 0 && a[j] > key){ a[j+1] = a[j]; j--; } a[j+1] = key; } }

problems.explanation: Swap me har step par 3 writes lagte hain, shifting me 1. Nearly sorted data par insertion sort bahut fast hai (isliye std::sort chhote partitions par isi ka use karta hai).

problems.title: Detect Capital Use
problems.problem_statement: Return true if the word uses capitals correctly: all capitals, no capitals, or only the first letter capital.
problems.description: Teen valid patterns: USA, leetcode, Google.
problems.theory: Uppercase letters ginno. Valid agar count 0, n, ya (count 1 aur pehla letter capital).

brute_force.approach: Teen variants (upper, lower, capitalized) banao aur word se compare.
brute_force.code_cpp: bool detectCapital(const string& w){ string u = w, l = w, c = w; for(char& x : u) x = toupper((unsigned char)x); for(char& x : l) x = tolower((unsigned char)x); for(size_t i = 0; i < c.size(); i++) c[i] = i ? tolower((unsigned char)c[i]) : toupper((unsigned char)c[i]); return w == u || w == l || w == c; }

optimized.code_cpp: bool detectCapital(const string& w){ int up = 0; for(char c : w) if(isupper((unsigned char)c)) up++; return up == 0 || up == (int)w.size() || (up == 1 && isupper((unsigned char)w[0])); }

problems.explanation: Dono O(n) hain; optimized extra strings nahi banata. Rule ko counting condition me badalna interview ka main skill hai.

problems.title: Reverse Words in a String III
problems.problem_statement: Reverse the characters of each word in the sentence while keeping word order and spaces.
problems.description: Words ek space se alag hain (no leading/trailing/multiple spaces).
problems.theory: Word ke start/end indices nikalo aur sirf us segment ko reverse karo.

brute_force.approach: stringstream se words, har word reverse, join.
brute_force.code_cpp: string revWords3(const string& s){ stringstream ss(s); string w, r; bool first = true; while(ss >> w){ reverse(w.begin(), w.end()); if(!first) r += ' '; r += w; first = false; } return r; }

optimized.code_cpp: string revWords3(string s){ int n = s.size(), i = 0; while(i < n){ int j = i; while(j < n && s[j] != ' ') j++; reverse(s.begin() + i, s.begin() + j); i = j + 1; } return s; }

problems.explanation: Reverse Words in a String (L1-019) se alag: yahan words ka order same rehta hai, sirf andar ke characters ulte hote hain.

problems.title: String Compression (In-place)
problems.problem_statement: Compress a character array in-place using run-length encoding: for each group of repeated characters, write the character followed by the group's length if length > 1. Return the new length.
problems.description: Group length >= 10 ho to digits alag characters me likhe jaate hain. Extra array allowed nahi.
problems.theory: Read pointer i group ki seema j tak jata hai; write pointer w character likhta hai, phir (length > 1 ho to) count ke digits. w kabhi i se aage nahi nikalta.

brute_force.approach: Naya string banao aur wapas array me copy karo.
brute_force.code_cpp: int compress(vector<char>& c){ string t; int n = c.size(), i = 0; while(i < n){ int j = i; while(j < n && c[j] == c[i]) j++; t += c[i]; if(j - i > 1) t += to_string(j - i); i = j; } for(size_t k = 0; k < t.size(); k++) c[k] = t[k]; return t.size(); }

optimized.code_cpp: int compress(vector<char>& c){ int n = c.size(), w = 0, i = 0; while(i < n){ int j = i; while(j < n && c[j] == c[i]) j++; c[w++] = c[i]; if(j - i > 1) for(char d : to_string(j - i)) c[w++] = d; i = j; } return w; }

problems.explanation: Safe kyun hai: length L >= 2 ki group ke liye likha hua part (1 + digits) hamesha L se chhota ya barabar hota hai, isliye unread characters overwrite nahi hote.

problems.title: Maximum Number of Balloons
problems.problem_statement: Return the maximum number of times the word 'balloon' can be formed using letters from text (each letter at most once).
problems.description: 'balloon' me l aur o do-do baar aate hain.
problems.theory: Frequency count: b/a/n jitne hain, l/o ka aadha. Answer in sabka minimum.

brute_force.approach: Baar baar 'balloon' ke letters text se find + erase karo jab tak fail na ho.
brute_force.code_cpp: int maxBalloons(string t){ int c = 0; for(;;){ for(char ch : string("balloon")){ size_t p = t.find(ch); if(p == string::npos) return c; t.erase(p, 1); } c++; } }

optimized.code_cpp: int maxBalloons(const string& t){ int f[26] = {0}; for(char c : t) f[c - 'a']++; return min({f['b'-'a'], f['a'-'a'], f['l'-'a'] / 2, f['o'-'a'] / 2, f['n'-'a']}); }

problems.explanation: Ransom Note ka special case: magazine = text, note = 'balloon' ki repeated copies. Bottleneck letter hi answer decide karta hai.
edge_cases: Many l and o but few b

problems.title: Integer Square Root (Sqrt of x)
problems.problem_statement: Given a non-negative integer x, return floor(sqrt(x)) without using built-in sqrt/pow.
problems.description: Answer integer part hi hai, decimal digits truncate hote hain.
problems.theory: Condition mid*mid <= x monotonic hai (true...true false...false), isliye binary search se sabse bada mid nikalo. mid*mid ke liye long long.

brute_force.code_cpp: int mySqrt(int x){ long long i = 0; while((i + 1) * (i + 1) <= x) i++; return (int)i; }

optimized.code_cpp: int mySqrt(int x){ long long lo = 0, hi = x, ans = 0; while(lo <= hi){ long long mid = (lo + hi) / 2; if(mid * mid <= x){ ans = mid; lo = mid + 1; } else hi = mid - 1; } return (int)ans; }

problems.explanation: Ye Level 2 ke 'Binary Search on Answer' pattern ka pehla example hai. Floating sqrt() precision issues de sakta hai bade x par.

problems.title: Armstrong Number
problems.problem_statement: A number with d digits is an Armstrong number if the sum of each digit raised to the power d equals the number. Check if n is Armstrong.
problems.theory: Pehle digits ki sankhya d nikalo, phir har digit ka d-th power (integer multiplication se) jodo.

brute_force.approach: to_string aur pow() ka use (floating point, round karna padta hai).
brute_force.code_cpp: bool isArm(int n){ string s = to_string(n); int d = s.size(); long long sum = 0; for(char c : s) sum += llround(pow(c - '0', d)); return sum == n; }

optimized.approach: Integer-only: digit count loop + power loop.
optimized.code_cpp: bool isArm(int n){ int d = 0; for(int x = n; x; x /= 10) d++; long long sum = 0; for(int x = n; x; x /= 10){ int dig = x % 10; long long p = 1; for(int i = 0; i < d; i++) p *= dig; sum += p; } return sum == n; }

problems.explanation: Integer approach me floating point error ka risk nahi. Chhote d ke liye O(d^2) negligible hai. n = 0 ko single-digit Armstrong maana jata hai.

problems.title: LCM of an Array
problems.problem_statement: Return the least common multiple of all numbers in the array.
problems.description: LCM wo sabse chhota number jo array ke har number se divisible ho.
problems.theory: lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b. Array par fold karo: l = lcm(l, a[i]). Pehle divide karke multiply karne se overflow kam hota hai.

brute_force.approach: Max element ke multiples try karo jab tak sab se divisible na ho.
brute_force.code_cpp: long long lcmArr(const vector<int>& a){ long long m = *max_element(a.begin(), a.end()); for(long long c = m;; c += m){ bool ok = true; for(int x : a) if(c % x){ ok = false; break; } if(ok) return c; } }

optimized.code_cpp: long long lcmArr(const vector<int>& a){ long long l = 1; for(int x : a) l = l / std::gcd(l, (long long)x) * x; return l; }

problems.explanation: Brute ka runtime answer ke size par depend karta hai (1..20 ka LCM 232792560 hai, to bahut slow). gcd fold me har step logarithmic hai.

problems.title: Perfect Number
problems.problem_statement: A perfect number equals the sum of its proper positive divisors (excluding itself). Check if n is perfect.
problems.theory: Divisors pairs me aate hain (i, n/i). i ko sqrt(n) tak chalao aur dono jodo (i == n/i ho to ek baar).

brute_force.approach: 1 se n-1 tak saare divisors jodo.
brute_force.code_cpp: bool isPerfect(int n){ if(n <= 1) return false; int s = 0; for(int i = 1; i < n; i++) if(n % i == 0) s += i; return s == n; }

optimized.code_cpp: bool isPerfect(int n){ if(n <= 1) return false; int s = 1; for(int i = 2; (long long)i * i <= n; i++) if(n % i == 0){ s += i; if(i != n / i) s += n / i; } return s == n; }

problems.explanation: 1e8 par brute lagbhag 1e8 operations leta hai, optimized sirf ~1e4. n = 1 ke liye proper divisors ka sum 0 hota hai, isliye false.

problems.title: N-th Tribonacci Number
problems.theory: Naive recursion me har call 3 aur calls banati hai (O(3^n)). Pichhli teen values rolling variables me rakho.

brute_force.code_cpp: int trib(int n){ if(n == 0) return 0; if(n <= 2) return 1; return trib(n - 1) + trib(n - 2) + trib(n - 3); }

optimized.code_cpp: int trib(int n){ if(n == 0) return 0; if(n <= 2) return 1; int a = 0, b = 1, c = 1; for(int i = 3; i <= n; i++){ int d = a + b + c; a = b; b = c; c = d; } return c; }

problems.explanation: Fibonacci -> Climbing Stairs -> Tribonacci ek hi DP family hai. Window of last k values rakhna sab me common hai.

problems.title: Reverse a String Using Recursion
problems.description: Loop ke bina recursion se reverse karna hai. Efficiency ka dhyan rakho.
problems.theory: Index-based recursion: swap(s[l], s[r]) karke (l+1, r-1) par recursion. Base case l >= r.

brute_force.approach: rev(s) = rev(s.substr(1)) + s[0]; har call par naya string copy hota hai.
brute_force.code_cpp: string revRec(const string& s){ if(s.size() <= 1) return s; return revRec(s.substr(1)) + s[0]; }

optimized.code_cpp:
void helper(string& s, int l, int r){ if(l >= r) return; swap(s[l], s[r]); helper(s, l + 1, r - 1); }
void revRec(string& s){ helper(s, 0, (int)s.size() - 1); }

problems.explanation: substr aur + operator dono naya string banate hain, isliye brute me hidden O(n) cost hai. Iterative two-pointer me stack space bhi O(1) rehti hai.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.problem_statement: Given a sorted array of distinct integers and a target, return the index of target or -1 if it does not exist. Use O(log n) time.
problems.description: Level 2 ke saare binary search patterns ki base.
problems.theory: Search space [lo, hi]. mid check karo: equal to return, chhota to right half (lo = mid+1), bada to left half (hi = mid-1).

brute_force.code_cpp: int searchLinear(const vector<int>& a, int t){ for(int i = 0; i < (int)a.size(); i++) if(a[i] == t) return i; return -1; }

optimized.code_cpp: int searchBinary(const vector<int>& a, int t){ int lo = 0, hi = (int)a.size() - 1; while(lo <= hi){ int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if(a[mid] == t) return mid; if(a[mid] < t) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid - 1; } return -1; }

problems.explanation: 1e4 elements par log2(1e4) ~ 14 steps lagte hain. Sorted hona precondition hai. Ye Level 1 aur Level 2 ke beech ka bridge hai.

pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: freq[26] ya unordered_map; ek ya do pass

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Palindrome, reverse, sorted pair sum, squares of sorted
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: l = 0, r = n-1; condition par move
k = write index; valid element par a[k++] = x

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Range ya left-right sum ke questions

pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: Peeche se likho taaki unread data overwrite na ho

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Pair cancel, set bits, power of two

pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b); lcm = a / gcd * b
i * i <= n par (i, n/i) pair
Last k values rakho, loop chalao

complexity_cheat_sheet.complexity: O(n^2) (insertion best O(n) on nearly sorted)

complexity_cheat_sheet.item: std::string concatenation s = s + c in a loop
complexity_cheat_sheet.complexity: O(n^2) overall; s += c is amortized O(1)

common_mistakes: Constraints padhe bina brute force ya optimization choose karna (n <= 1e5 par O(n^2) TLE deta hai)
Edge cases miss: empty input, n = 1, all same, negatives, zeros, INT_MIN/INT_MAX
int overflow: sums/products ke liye long long, mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
Two pointers me pointers cross hone ke baad access ya skip loop me boundary check na lagana
Hash map me insert pehle kar dena jabki complement/same-index check baad me hona chahiye
Input array in-place modify hone ki baat batana bhool jana (interviewer ko mention karo)
char se seedha index banana (negative ho sakta hai), (unsigned char) cast lagao
Output mein 0-based vs 1-based index ka confusion
interview_checklist: 1. Problem ko apne words me repeat karo aur examples se confirm karo
2. Constraints puchho (n ka size, value range, duplicates, sorted?, negatives?)
3. Brute force bolo aur uski complexity batao
4. Bottleneck pehchano (repeated work? search? sorting?) aur pattern chuno
5. Optimized approach explain karo, code likhne se pehle small example par dry run karo
6. Code likho: clear variable names, helper functions
7. Edge cases par test karo (empty, single, duplicates, extremes)
8. Time aur space complexity bolo; agar possible ho to trade-offs batao
cpp_tips: vector<int>::size() unsigned hota hai: i - 1 ya size() - 1 par underflow dhyan rakho, int cast karo
reverse(a.begin() + i, a.begin() + j) half-open range [i, j) reverse karta hai
unordered_map ka operator[] missing key insert kar deta hai, find()/count() se check karo
string ke liye to_string(), stoi(), stoll(); char ke liye c - '0' aur c - 'a'
__builtin_popcount(x) set bits, std::gcd(a, b) (C++17) built-in hain, par interview me algorithm explain karna padta hai
long long literal: 1LL << k, aur multiplication se pehle cast: (long long)a * b

self_test_before_level_2.instruction: Bina solution dekhe, har problem ka brute + optimized approach 10 minute me explain kar sako to Level 2 ke liye ready ho.
